operations.name: Suggest options from a website
operations.agentTask: Read the website in `sourceUrl` and write three different ways to fill the ad "Macro feature proof". Objective: Show a specific hardware or product detail, then explain why it matters. Visual rule: Extreme detail turns into a useful, understandable product benefit. Beats, in order: - 0–1.8 s: Feature detail dominates the frame. Shows Brand color, Close-up, Feature name. - 1.8–4.5 s: Demonstrate one actual feature state. Shows Brand color, Close-up, What it does. - 4.5–7 s: Reveal the full product. Shows Brand color, Full product, Benefit. - 7–8.5 s: Hold concise benefit and any necessary qualification. Shows Brand color, Full product, Benefit with proof. - 8.5–10 s: Product, brand and CTA. Shows Brand color, Full product, Logo, Call to action. Use only facts the website or pages you read state. Never invent prices, discounts, dates, guarantees or claims. When a fact a field needs is missing, write a short placeholder in square brackets, such as [offer end date]. Make the three options clearly different in angle, wording and image choice. For images, choose real, large images of this brand and product: first from the page's own images (header logo, large files, feature-page screenshots), then with an image search. A social preview card (og:image, a title on a gradient) is a last resort. Give the direct URL of the image file, never a page URL, and never an image of another brand. Use an empty string when no image fits. If image search throws because no search backend is configured, tell the user in one sentence that a SerpAPI, DataForSEO or Brave key in Settings finds better images. Then take nodetool.web.screenshot of the product's feature pages instead. Save each image you consider as an asset and look at it with view_image before you offer it. Name in the option's description any image that is only a social preview card. Write `fillOptions` as a list of three objects, `fillChoice` as "" and `fillReport` as "". Each option: - value: "1", "2" or "3" - title: a name for the direction in 2 to 4 words - description: one sentence on what it emphasizes, then the first two copy lines in quotes - image: the URL of its first image, for the option card - brandColor: the brand's accent color as #RRGGBB (buttons, links, highlights), not the page background or a theme-color that is near black or white - fields: featureName (Feature name: macro hook, at most 7 words); featureAction (What it does: demonstration, at most 7 words); benefit (Benefit: context, at most 7 words); qualifiedBenefit (Benefit with proof: proof, at most 16 words); cta (Call to action: cta, at most 4 words) - images: macroDetail (Close-up: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: Feature detail dominates the frame. | Demonstrate one actual feature state.); fullProduct (Full product: A shot of the product alone, ideally on a plain or transparent background, so it reads as a cutout. Shown in: Reveal the full product. | Hold concise benefit and any necessary qualification. | Product, brand and CTA.); logo (Logo: The brand's own logo file, such as the site header logo or its icon. Shown in: Product, brand and CTA.) Then show the Start step with `only: ["fillChoice"]` and a one-sentence note, so the user sees just the option cards. Picking one runs `apply`, which saves the images and fills the steps.
